claims.text: Adding a small amount of Al to Co-free FeNiCrMn will improve its dynamic mechanical performance.
The proposed improvement will occur from -20°C to 200°C and at strain rates from 10^(-3) s^(-1) to 10^3 s^(-1).
Al addition will form a stable, coherent nanoprecipitate phase in the FeNiCrMn matrix.
The coherent nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation movement.
Impeded dislocation movement will enhance strength and resistance to dynamic deformation.
Al addition will promote grain refinement in FeNiCrMn.
Al addition will reduce void and crack formation in FeNiCrMn.
Al-modified FeNiCrMn will have higher yield strength than unmodified FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading.
Al-modified FeNiCrMn will have higher ultimate tensile strength than unmodified FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading.
Al-modified FeNiCrMn will have greater ductility than unmodified FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading.
The improvement will be most pronounced near 100°C and a strain rate of 10^1 s^(-1).
The optimal amount of Al is uncertain.
The composition and morphology of the proposed nanoprecipitates are uncertain.
A split-Hopkinson-bar tensile experiment comparing Al-modified and unmodified FeNiCrMn can test the predicted dynamic response.
Failure to obtain at least a 10% improvement in yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, or ductility will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and ductility all to improve, whereas the use of 'or' in the falsification rule is ambiguous and may allow improvement in only one property to prevent falsification.

The stated range extends down to a quasi-static strain rate of 10^(-3) s^(-1), but a split-Hopkinson-bar experiment alone ordinarily addresses high-rate loading and therefore does not test the full claimed range.
